previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted for a flare of chronic pancreatitis, presenting with epigastric pain radiating to the back, nausea, and vomiting. She was treated with IV fluids, hydromorphone, ketorolac, and anti-nausea medications, with gradual advancement to a soft diet. Her pain and nausea improved, and she was transitioned back to oral medications. New concerns included dental caries, particularly in tooth #8, prompting a referral to oral surgery for planned extractions with antibiotic prophylaxis. Anticoagulation with lovenox was stopped after completing treatment for a prior line-associated DVT. Blood pressure was managed with continued amlodipine and addition of lisinopril. She was discharged home with home health services, instructions for Hickman line care with ethanol locks, and follow-up plans for dental and primary care.

radiology_notes.text:
PA AND LATERAL CHEST ___:

HISTORY:  Fever and no cough or crackles.

IMPRESSION:  PA and lateral chest compared to chest radiographs since ___, most recently ___:

Tip of the right central venous catheter is at or just above the expected
level of the superior cavoatrial junction.  Lungs are fully expanded and
clear.  Cardiomediastinal and hilar silhouettes and pleural surfaces are all
normal.  I see no explanation in the chest for fever.

INDICATION:  ___ female with fever.  Assess right arm for DVT.

COMPARISON:  Right arm ultrasound ___.

FINDINGS:  Gray scale, color and Doppler images were obtained of the right IJ,
subclavian, axillary, brachial, basilic veins.  Normal flow, compression, and
augmentation is seen in all of the deep veins of the right arm and also in the
right basilic vein.  Note is made that the right cephalic vein could not be
identified.

IMPRESSION:  No evidence of deep vein thrombosis in the right arm.

LIVER ULTRASOUND

INDICATION:  A ___ female with rising liver function tests,
Gram-negative bacteremia, and known chronic pancreatitis.  Scan to assess for
possible biliary obstruction.

The patient is status post cholecystectomy.  The common hepatic duct is at the
upper limits of normal in size measuring 5 mm in diameter and the common bile
duct shows normal tapering as it extends into the head of the pancreas,
measuring 4 mm in maximal diameter.  There is no evidence of intrahepatic bile
duct dilatation and no stones are seen within the biliary tree.  The liver is
normal in size and echogenicity with no focal lesions identified.  Portal vein
is patent with forward flow.  The spleen, however, appears mildly enlarged
measuring 12-12.9 cm in length.  Limited views of the head and proximal body
of the pancreas are normal, but the distal body and tail are completely
obscured by overlying bowel gas.  Within the area of visualization, the
pancreatic duct does not appear dilated.  The common bile duct is seen in the
pancreatic head at the region of the ampulla and is normal in appearance.

Limited views of the aorta, inferior vena cava, right and left kidneys are
unremarkable.  There is no evidence of ascites.

CONCLUSION:  Mild splenomegaly is noted, but study is otherwise normal. 
Status post cholecystectomy.

EXAM:  MRI of the mandibles.

CLINICAL INFORMATION:  Rule out osteomyelitis of the jaw.

TECHNIQUE:  T1 and T2 axial and inversion recovery coronal images of the
sinuses and mandible were obtained.  Following gadolinium, T1 axial and
coronal images acquired.

FINDINGS:  There is no evidence of abnormal signal identified in the region of
mandible or the maxilla.  Artifacts slightly limit the evaluation of the
maxilla in the left molar region.  The artifacts appear to be from the dental
hardware.  There is no soft tissue swelling seen adjacent to the maxilla or
mandible or evidence of fluid collection identified to indicate abscess. 
There are no bony signal abnormalities indicative of osteomyelitis.  The
visualized sinuses are clear.  There are slightly prominent but not
pathologically enlarged nodes visualized in both submandibular region.  No
other significantly enlarged lymph nodes are identified in the upper neck. 
The nasopharyngeal soft tissues and oropharyngeal soft tissues are symmetric.

IMPRESSION:  No MRI signs of osteomyelitis in the mandible or maxilla.  Dental
artifacts slightly limit evaluation in the left maxillary region.  Other
findings as above.  No fluid collection or abscess seen.

STUDY:  Panorex view ___.

___. MRI ___.

INDICATION:  Question osteomyelitis, compared to prior Panorex.

ADDITIONAL INFORMATION:  Poor dentition, concern for bacteremia related to jaw
infection.

FINDINGS AND IMPRESSION: No definite fractures.  No periapical lucencies
identified.  Multiple lucencies within the teeth, likely representing caries. 
No definite periostitis.  No definite cortical destruction.

IMPRESSION:
1.  No definite osteomyelitis. Multiple caries.
2.  MRI is more sensitive to evaluate for osteomyelitis.  Compared to MRI from
yesterday.
